summary: Equity medians: US large cap 6.3% (n=7), US small cap 6.0% (n=6), global equity 6.8% (n=5) and EM equity 8.1% (n=6, range down to 3.0%); private equity has the highest median, 9.7% (n=5).

Fixed income medians: US cash 3.6% (n=6), US aggregate 4.6% (n=6), intermediate Treasuries 4.8% (n=7), US IG corporates 5.2% (n=5), high yield 5.5% (n=7), EM USD sovereigns 5.7% (n=8); all IQRs 90bp or less.
Widest disagreements, ranked by IQR among rows with n≥4: commodities 225bp (n=7), US small cap 188bp (n=6), private equity 155bp (n=5), private credit 143bp (n=4), EM equity 122bp (n=6).

US large cap stances: BlackRock Investment Institute (high conviction) and Goldman Sachs AM overweight on AI earnings; PIMCO (vanishing equity risk premium), Lazard (rotation away from US equities) and Amundi underweight, each low conviction.
Where n≥4, this site's LTCMA departs most from public medians on commodities (3.5% vs 5.2%, 170bp below) and US TIPS (4.5% vs 3.8%, 72bp above); high yield and EM local debt sit 50bp below.
The largest gaps involve thin rows: this site's LTCMA has UK equity at 7.0% vs 9.0% from two publishers (191bp below) and gold at 3.3% vs 1.6% from a single publisher (170bp above).

Prediction markets (Kalshi, Polymarket): next-FOMC no change 82.5-83.0%, 25bp hike 16.5% on both, zero cuts this year 95.7-95.8%, at odds with the easing calls of Goldman Sachs AM, UBS GWM CIO and Mercer.

A US recession this year is priced at 3.5% (Kalshi) and 6.5% (Polymarket), in line with most managers' expansion base cases; hike odds fit Vanguard's higher-for-longer Fed, while BlackRock Investment Institute sees hikes overpriced.

divergence_rule: public IQR >= 150bp with n >= 4, or >= 1 overweight and >= 1 underweight stance

divergences.label: US large cap
divergences.headline: US large cap: 4.9-7.6% range around a 6.3% median (n=7) splits on valuation drag versus AI-driven earnings.

bull.argument: BNY Investments (7.6%, top of range) sums income, inflation, real GDP growth and AI-driven profit-share gains, valuations held flat; Fidelity International adds AI-lifted revenue, dividends and share repurchases net of a margin drag. Goldman Sachs AM and BlackRock Investment Institute are overweight on AI-driven earnings power. T. Rowe Price edges above the median despite citing rich growth valuations.
bull.data_used: Income, inflation and real earnings growth, with AI lifting revenues and profit share; valuations held constant or only modestly penalized.

bear.argument: Starting valuations dominate: Invesco (4.9%, bottom of range) sees real earnings growth and shareholder yield overwhelmed by multiple compression; Vanguard and State Street also cut returns for elevated valuations. PIMCO, underweight, sees a vanishing equity risk premium and better prospective Sharpe ratios in bonds; Lazard expects rotation out of US equities, doubting US resilience. Amundi is also underweight.
bear.data_used: Elevated starting multiples with assumed mean reversion, the equity risk premium versus bond yields, and doubts about US growth resilience.

divergences.what_to_watch: Whether AI-linked earnings growth keeps pace with multiples: mega-cap forward earnings revisions versus P/E, and the earnings yield's spread over Treasury yields.

divergences.label: US small cap
divergences.headline: US small cap: widest equity IQR (188bp, n=6); views split on small-cap earnings growth and starting valuations.

bull.argument: BNY Investments (7.5%, top of range) sees a slim size premium because firms stay private longer, leaving small caps just under broad US equity; AQR's real-return build lands well above the median. T. Rowe Price selectively raised its small-cap expectation. Goldman Sachs AM, overweight, cites appealing valuations, anticipated Fed cuts, faster profit growth and reviving deal activity.
bull.data_used: Factor-model size premium, local real-return estimates plus inflation, relative valuations, and an assumed Fed easing path with M&A recovery.

bear.argument: Invesco (4.5%, bottom of range) sees a lighter valuation penalty than in large caps offset by weak long-run profit growth, ranking small caps behind mid-caps. Vanguard says the strong rally lifted valuations and trimmed expected returns much as in large caps; State Street also lands below the median, expecting higher volatility.
bear.data_used: Post-rally starting valuations, weak long-run small-cap earnings growth, and higher expected volatility.

divergences.what_to_watch: Small-cap earnings growth relative to large caps, and whether the rate cuts Goldman Sachs AM expects arrive; zero cuts this year are priced at 95.7-95.8% across venues.

divergences.label: US high yield
divergences.headline: US high yield: 4.6-6.1% range (n=7) splits on whether high carry outweighs tight spreads and rising defaults.

bull.argument: Carry dominates even after haircuts: Invesco and BNY Investments (both 6.1%, top of range) start from high all-in yields and net off expected credit losses and spread widening. Fidelity International sees spread income only partly offset by default losses. Goldman Sachs AM, overweight, cites healthy interest coverage, contained defaults, an upgraded ratings mix, solid demand and M&A support.
bull.data_used: Starting all-in yield minus expected default losses and spread-widening haircuts; issuer fundamentals such as interest coverage and ratings mix, plus demand and M&A.

bear.argument: Tight spreads underpay for risk: State Street (4.6%, bottom of range) sees default-adjusted spreads leaving little extra return over IG; Vanguard judges credit expensive; AQR also sits below the median. PIMCO, underweight, reads near-record-tight spreads as complacent while defaults climb and leans toward higher quality. Amundi is also underweight.
bear.data_used: Current spreads versus history, the spread term structure and default probabilities, and an emerging rise in defaults.

divergences.what_to_watch: Speculative-grade default rates and HY spreads: rising defaults with spreads still near historic tights would vindicate the lower estimates; contained defaults would favor the carry view.

divergences.label: Commodities
divergences.headline: Commodities: widest IQR of any row (225bp, n=7); estimates hinge on futures risk premium and roll-return assumptions.

bull.argument: AQR (6.7%, top of range) adds a persistent long-run excess return of equal-weighted commodity futures over cash to its expected cash return. Robeco ties outcomes to conflicts and the dollar, within a base case of investment-led expansion with higher inflation. Vanguard's figure is pure model output, above the median but without commodity-specific commentary despite higher energy prices.
bull.data_used: Long-run excess return of diversified futures over cash, expected cash (collateral) returns, inflation, and geopolitical and dollar drivers.

bear.argument: BNY Investments (2.3%, bottom of range) projects weak returns with high volatility and gives no drivers. State Street combines inflation and dollar projections with long-run roll and collateral returns. Invesco nudged its view up on a more supportive real-asset outlook yet stays below the median, stressing commodities' distinct diversifying return sources.
bear.data_used: Inflation and dollar forecasts, long-term roll return and collateral return; BNY Investments discloses no rationale.

divergences.what_to_watch: Realized roll yield (backwardation versus contango), T-bill yields that set collateral return, and the dollar's path, which Robeco and State Street both cite.

divergences.label: Global govt bonds
divergences.headline: Global govt bonds: tight 23bp IQR (n=3) masks a directional split over fiscal strain versus income and diversification.

bull.argument: Robeco (5.3%, top of range, developed sovereigns hedged to USD) says higher yields have improved expected returns, though not without risk. PIMCO, overweight with high conviction, expects out-of-sync economies and divergent central-bank paths to open country and curve opportunities, with global sovereigns adding income and diversification.
bull.data_used: Current sovereign yields hedged to USD, cross-country divergence in cycles and monetary policy, and curve shape.

bear.argument: BNY Investments, underweight, argues fiscal strain may weaken sovereign bonds' risk-adjusted appeal and looks to real assets and private markets for diversification. Fidelity International is here only on its number (4.8%, bottom of range); it is overweight, expecting income from higher curves and diversification in recessionary shocks.
bear.data_used: Fiscal strain on sovereign balance sheets and risk-adjusted comparison with real assets and private markets; for Fidelity, income from higher yield curves.

divergences.what_to_watch: Term premia and long-end yields under fiscal pressure, and whether sovereigns rally in the next growth scare or fall alongside risk assets.

divergences.label: Private equity
divergences.headline: Private equity: 6.6-10.5% range (n=5) turns on whether an illiquidity premium survives fees and leverage costs.

bull.argument: BNY Investments (10.5%, top of range), overweight, adds a sizable illiquidity premium to public-equity factor exposure, arguing private capital is financing AI-related innovation and infrastructure. T. Rowe Price ranks private equity top among its forecasts on illiquidity and active-management advantages over listed equity.
bull.data_used: Public-equity factor exposure plus an assumed illiquidity premium, manager skill, and private-capital demand from AI and infrastructure build-outs.

bear.argument: AQR (6.6%, bottom of range) models US private equity as levered equity in a dividend-discount framework net of sizable fees; cheaper debt and multiple expansion lifted its estimate, yet it sees private-asset risk premia compressed against positive real cash and bond yields. State Street uses PE's historical performance versus listed equity, leverage-adjusted and net of fees.
bear.data_used: Levered dividend-discount model with fee drag and debt costs; leverage-adjusted historical private-equity returns versus listed equities.

divergences.what_to_watch: Distributions and exit activity versus reported marks, acquisition financing costs, and whether net private-equity returns keep a margin over public equity after fees.

divergences.label: Private credit
divergences.headline: Private credit: overweights outnumber PIMCO's high-conviction underweight; estimates span 5.0-9.2% (n=4) on fees and defaults.

bull.argument: T. Rowe Price (9.2%, top of range) cites an illiquidity premium and lasting demand for private capital; Fidelity International sees higher rates lifting net-of-fee income and no immediate stress. Goldman Sachs AM, BlackRock Investment Institute and Amundi are overweight; Goldman cites extra yield over public credit and lower historical defaults than syndicated loans, BII lender protections and recovery value.
bull.data_used: Floating-rate income at elevated base rates, illiquidity premium, historical default rates versus syndicated loans, and underwriting and lender-protection quality.

bear.argument: AQR (5.0%, bottom of range) treats direct lending as modestly levered floating-rate high yield whose illiquidity premium is consumed by fees, with narrower spreads and lower cash rates cutting returns. PIMCO, underweight, sees middle-market stress in extended maturities, payment-in-kind usage and financial engineering, and flags recovery risk, while favoring asset-based finance. State Street also sits below the median.
bear.data_used: Modeled levered high yield net of fees, spread compression and lower cash rates; observed payment-in-kind usage, maturity extensions and recovery prospects.

divergences.what_to_watch: Direct-lending non-accruals, payment-in-kind share of income and realized recoveries; rising stress would support PIMCO's underweight, stable credit quality the overweights.

regimes.cycle_phase: Resilient growth; inflation-focused central banks; higher-for-longer Fed; stretched valuations after Q2 risk rally
regimes.summary: Sharp Q2 rally in risk assets stretched equity valuations and lowered expected returns; sovereign yields stable, credit rich. No explicit risk tilt; valuations not deemed a basis for reallocating.

regimes.cycle_phase: No cycle call; valuation-based view after a third straight equity rally, with rich US equities and positive real cash rates.
regimes.summary: No market-timing call. Risk premia look compressed for equities and private assets relative to positive real cash and bond yields, and AQR expects lower equity excess returns.

regimes.cycle_phase: Resilient growth, moderating inflation, elevated yields; uncertain and possibly hawkish policy path
regimes.summary: Elevated valuations temper US equity returns; non-US developed markets look relatively better; higher yields lift bond expectations, narrowing the equity-bond gap and reinforcing fixed income diversification.

regimes.cycle_phase: Mid-cycle: rejuvenated expansion, less late-cycle than widely believed
regimes.summary: Base case Great Rewiring (50%): AI- and investment-led rejuvenated expansion with higher inflation, supportive for risk-taking; bull Luminous Renaissance 15%, bear Synaptic Decay 35%.

regimes.cycle_phase: Late cycle: resilient but downside-skewed growth, with a credit default cycle now beginning amid geopolitical rupture
regimes.summary: Geopolitical rupture, fragmentation, fiscal strain and an AI capex boom widen outcome tails; PIMCO favors resilience over reach via high-quality, globally diversified bonds and up-in-quality credit.

regimes.cycle_phase: Not explicitly stated; fragile growth and structural transition amid the Iran-war shock
regimes.summary: Beyond Iran headlines, Lazard sees structural shifts: a weaker dollar, improving non-US equity relative performance, and steeper developed-market curves, while US economic resilience looks increasingly doubtful.

regimes.cycle_phase: Mid-cycle; soft landing with policy easing
regimes.summary: Soft-landing base case: gradual Fed easing with possibly two cuts in 2026; credit mid-cycle; easing, AI capex and dealmaking are catalysts amid elevated valuations and fiscal risks.
risks: AI capex disappointment and market concentration

regimes.cycle_phase: Expansion: uneven growth entering 2026, improving through the year as confidence recovers, fiscal stimulus gains traction, tariff effects fade and the Fed eases.
regimes.summary: Constructive: supportive economic backdrop for stocks, AI capex and adoption driving gains, Fed easing toward 3.33%, weaker dollar; political noise seen as short-lived for markets.

regimes.cycle_phase: Structural paradigm shift from globalization to modern mercantilism, combined with an AI capex boom and resource grab
regimes.summary: Bridgewater sees a new regime shaped by national self-interest and AI investment. AI capex supports US growth, but inflation risks are structurally higher, and portfolios built for the old era are fragile.

regimes.cycle_phase: Steady expansion with broadly easing policy; growth, inflation and rates converging toward long-term averages
regimes.summary: Mercer expects steady 2026 global growth led by a resilient, AI- and fiscally-supported US, inflation near targets and easing policy, keeping overall market positioning broadly neutral.
risks: US policy uncertainty and Fed independence

regimes.cycle_phase: Growth re-accelerating into 2026 with fiscal and monetary support, as policy diverges across regions
regimes.summary: Moderately constructive long-run view: AI productivity lifts equity and private-market returns, while fiscal strain, steeper curves and a weaker dollar favor global diversification over sovereign duration.
risks: Weak demand for long-duration government bonds

regimes.cycle_phase: Stabilizing, more balanced but still uncertain phase after markets absorbed higher rates
regimes.summary: Markets have absorbed higher rates and activity has stabilized; valuations mostly normalized but elevated in US growth; returns stable to modestly lower, fixed income less forgiving.

regimes.cycle_phase: Not specified; long-term structural regime of geopolitical fragmentation and AI-driven growth with elevated inflation and volatility
regimes.summary: Fragmentation, high debt and tech/energy transitions keep macro volatility and inflation above pre-Covid norms; AI lifts long-run GDP growth, supporting equities while bonds stay attractive.

regimes.cycle_phase: Expansion with renewed Fed tightening: strong US growth and AI buildout, softer jobs data, and long yields at their highest since 2002.
regimes.summary: BII stays risk-on, overweighting US and EM equities on AI-driven earnings; sees markets overpricing Fed hikes, a dollar above fundamentals with limited upside, and structurally elevated long yields.
